ticket.description:
STEPS 1-6 OF 7 DONE. The crate exists (common/crates/gaugeblock-git, 7 modules, 30 fixture tests on real repositories and bare remotes) and the migration is complete in substance: git call sites in library sources went 68 -> 7, of which 1 is the crate itself, 4 are test fixtures that build scenario repositories, and 2 are documented exceptions (git add -A in outfeed restaging, whose semantics are a GB-150 decision; and outfeed git log --format carrying the commit body, which the crate Commit does not model yet).

API: repo identity (discover, common_dir, is_worktree, head_sha, current_branch incl. unborn HEAD, is_dirty, status_porcelain), worktrees (list/add/add-detached/remove/prune), history (commits_between, merge_base, is_ancestor, describe_tags, ahead_behind), index (stage_paths refusing an empty scope, commit returning CommitSummary, has_staged_changes, checkout, checkout_new_branch, pull_ff_only, restore_path, is_tracked), remote (tag_annotated, push_branch, push_branch_and_tag atomic, fetch_tag, remotes) and Repository::clone.

MIGRATED, one commit per repository: outfeed-core (git/mod + git/history + push + sync + sync_model + clone + manifest + lockfiles), storypole-core (git.rs), miter-engine (analysis/dirty, inventory/git_extractor) and miter-harness (sandbox create/mod/files, whose generic git() escape hatch is gone).

BEHAVIOUR CHANGES ON PURPOSE: outfeed push is now one atomic branch+tag push instead of two, so a rejected tag cannot leave a branch published and a release half-made; a detached HEAD is an InvalidBranch rather than the literal string; unborn HEAD reports its branch (a fix the migration itself surfaced).

REMAINING: step 7, the Tier 3 gate (miter contracts + chalkline docs check), and the two documented exceptions above if they are to be closed.

Every repository migrated with its own gate green
Worktree, history, index and remote verbs covered by fixture tests on real repositories

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-131 — `gaugeblock-git`

> **Scope:** `common/crates/gaugeblock-git` **Parent epic:** `GB-128` **Status:** Planned

## 1. Why this crate exists

Six places currently spawn `git` with `format!`-built command lines and parse stdout by hand:

| Owner | Duplicated calls |
|:--|:--|
| `storypole-core::git` | current branch, head sha, merge base, `rev-list` between shas |
| `outfeed-core::git` | dirty tree, commit + annotated tag, push, tag verify |
| `benchwork-core` | dirty tree, head sha, scoped commit for Panel 1 |
| `miter` (`deps --since`) | commit ranges |
| `rabbet` (backfill) | commit ranges, head sha |
| `scripts/*.sh` | branch, tags |

`GB-126` already collapsed the worst copy inside `outfeed`. This ticket generalizes the winner and
relocates it, it does not write a seventh wrapper.

## 2. Boundary (frozen — see `common/ARCHITECTURE.md` §4)

**Owns:** repository detection (`common_dir`, worktree vs main checkout), `worktree add/remove/prune/list`,
`rev-list`/`merge_base`/tag ranges, scoped `status`/`add`/`commit`/annotated `tag`, `push`.

**Does not own:** which repository to act on, `.gaugeblock/` resolution, workspace config, and any suite
type (`TaskNode`, `ReleasePlan`). A caller hands it a `Path` and typed arguments; it returns values or a
`thiserror` error carrying stderr. It never depends on `gaugeblock-workspace` — the edge is one-way
(`GB-189` -> `GB-131`).

## 3. Steps

| # | Step | Gate |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `repo` module: `common_dir`, `is_worktree`, `head_sha`, `current_branch`, `is_dirty` | `cargo nextest -p gaugeblock-git` with a temp repo + linked worktree fixture |
| 2 | `worktree` module: `add`, `remove`, `prune`, `list` returning typed `WorktreeInfo` | fixture asserts two worktrees share one `common_dir` |
| 3 | `history` module: `commits_between`, `merge_base`, `describe_range` (replaces `rev-list` string parsing) | fixture with a 3-commit range |
| 4 | `index` module: scoped `stage_paths` + `commit` returning a typed `CommitSummary` | fixture asserts only the named paths are staged (`GB-150` staging rule) |
| 5 | `remote` module: annotated `tag` + single-round-trip `push_branch_and_tag` | dry-run against a local bare remote |
| 6 | Delete `storypole-core::git`, `outfeed-core::git` and the benchwork copy; re-point callers | `cargo nextest --workspace` in each affected repo |
| 7 | `miter contracts` + `chalkline docs check` green | Tier 3 |

## 4. Consumers this unblocks

* `GB-169` — canonical `.gaugeblock` across worktrees needs step 2 and step 1 in that order.
* `GB-170` — benchwork agent pool needs `worktree add/remove/prune/list`.
* `GB-180` — Panel 1 atomic doc commits need step 4 (scoped staging, no `git add .`).
* `outfeed release` — needs step 5 for the single push.

## 5. Explicitly out of scope

* `codegen-units` tuning — moved to `GB-190` because it is a profile decision, not a crate boundary.
* Path/topology/config policy — `GB-189`.

plan.design_markdown:
# Task Plan: GB-131 — Extract gaugeblock-git Porcelain and Standardize codegen-units for Release Compilation

> **Task Key:** `GB-131`  
> **Parent Epic:** `GB-128`  
> **Scope:** `workspace`  
> **Status:** Planned

---

## 1. Problem Statement
`outfeed-core` has a 99.2% clone between single-repo and suite release tagging, and 4 tools duplicate git subprocess wrappers. Furthermore, all 10 repositories set `[profile.release] codegen-units = 1`, forcing LLVM to serialize to a single CPU core and slowing release compilations by 3x–5x.

---

## 2. Technical Blueprint
1. In `gaugeblock/common/crates/gaugeblock-git`:
   * Implement robust git porcelain helpers: `get_current_branch`, `is_working_tree_dirty`, `get_head_sha`, `create_commit_and_tag`.
   * Implement single-round-trip pushing (`push_branch_and_tag` -> `git push <remote> <branch> <tag>`).
2. In all 10 repository root `Cargo.toml` files:
   * Remove `codegen-units = 1` from `[profile.release]` (allowing default 16), or define a dedicated `release-dist` profile for CI packaging while keeping local release compilation multi-threaded.

---

## 3. Execution Steps
* **Step 1:** Implement git porcelain helpers in `gaugeblock-git`.
* **Step 2:** Standardize `[profile.release]` codegen-units across all 10 root Cargo.toml files.
* **Step 3:** Tier 3 workspace verification (`cargo nextest run --workspace`).

events.title: Extract gaugeblock-git: repository, worktree and ref-range process boundary
events.description: One crate owns everything that spawns git or reasons about a repository, lifted out of the four to six places that currently copy it. Ownership: common_dir and worktree detection (.git file versus directory, git rev-parse --git-common-dir); worktree add/remove/prune/list, which is what GB-169 and GB-170 need; rev-list and tag/commit ranges for storypole verify receipts, miter deps --since and rabbet backfill; scoped status/add/commit and annotated tag with single-round-trip push for outfeed release tagging and benchwork Panel 1 atomic doc commits (GB-180). Non-goals: it resolves no .gaugeblock path, chooses no repository, reads no workspace config and knows no suite vocabulary - that is gaugeblock-workspace (GB-189). Commands take typed arguments and return typed values or thiserror errors carrying stderr; no format!-built command lines. The codegen-units half of the old scope moved to GB-190 so this ticket is one crate.
acceptance_criteria: gaugeblock-git owns common_dir/worktree detection, worktree add/remove/prune/list, rev-list and tag ranges, and scoped status/add/commit/tag/push
gaugeblock-git does not depend on gaugeblock-workspace and resolves no .gaugeblock path
storypole-core::git, outfeed-core::git and the other git subprocess wrappers are deleted in favour of it
miter contracts and chalkline docs check stay green after the move
